items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Paul Burnett who had played banjo in Arthur Gibbs orchestra when I first heard him at the Savoy, was now playing guitar with Monnegue.

ctx.x: Whenever I am improvising on a tune which I have played before, it's very important for me not to remember what I did the last time I played it. I never think of what I did beforehand. It comes to me instantly. This is a question of knowing your instrument and what key you're playing in. It takes a long time to acquire, but once you know it, it's not difficult. It's like writing a letter. You write to your sister, and then you write to your brother, but you dont say the same thing, that's the way it is with…

I went into a dancing school for the first time with a pianist named Johnny Monnegue with Paul Barnes, alto sax, Jimmy Wright, tenor sax, Paul Burnett who had played banjo in Arthur Gibbs orchestra when I first heard him at the Savoy, was now playing guitar with Monnegue. The other trumpet man was Theodore 'Ted' Colin whom I had seen at the Rhythm Club many times. Ted was the loudest blowing trumpet player I have ever known and he did not blow out of tune which is blasting when a guy plays loud and not in tune.…

Working in a dancing school was not as interesting as working at the Savoy, Roseland or any other ballroom and the work was harder and especially with Monnegue. For one thing, the band was smaller. I don't remember who the drummer was and there was no bass. We were working in a dancing school on Broadway which was situated on the second floor of the building, just next door to the Roseland. The job started at 8 p.m. and finished at 2 a.m.
